findings.evidence: qa.feet: combo3 footL flat with 48 deg yaw while planted (drift 2.3 cm); combo1 footR 17 deg; combo2 footR 21.9 deg. qa.jointLimits footR.z: guard 38 deg (100%), walkF 45.2 (46%), walkB 49.2 (48%), slam 62 (65%), hit 46.9 (52%). Settled drift otherwise <= 2 mm in walks (moonwalk ratio <= 0.02) and <= 2.4 cm in attacks; landing skid <= 5 cm.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `pivot: 'ball' | 'heel'` to foot targets (rotate about that point, lift the other end). Raise the heel (toe roll) when dorsiflexion would exceed about 30 deg.

findings.title: Automatic pelvis drop is discontinuous: demo.combo3 drops the whole body 0.54 m and pops it back 0.50 m in one frame (twice per spin)
findings.detail: src/char/index.js:319-337 pelvisDrop(). When a foot target lies outside the leg reach, the drop is drop = dy - sqrt(R^2 - hz^2), which tends to the full hip height as hz approaches R (R = 0.97 x (thigh + shin)). As soon as hz >= R the foot is skipped (`|| hz2 >= R * R) continue;`), so the drop jumps from about 0.5 m to 0 in a single frame. It also applies to LIFTED swing feet: during the spin the right foot is 0.13-0.34 m above the floor. The function is called in resolve() (index.js:282) and again for the re-plant (index.js:628). In combo3 the right foot circles the pivot at 0.79 m. Hips model y goes 0.888 -> 0.346 m between t=0.367 and 0.433 (the knight collapses into a near-split), then +503 mm in ONE frame at t=0.45, then -428 mm in one frame at t=0.6167. The same pops occur inside the natural chain combo1>combo2>combo3 (t=2.25-2.53). Every secondary sim inherits the pop: tasset tip 31.6 m/s, cape jerk 592 mm/frame^2, cape edge stretch 3.6-4.2x. The result is very sensitive to the foot path: scaling the swing-foot circle by 0.8 / 0.7 / 0.6 / 0.4 gives pops of 391 / 547 / 105 / 31 mm. Any of the ~150-200 future clips with a foot near full reach (lunges, sweeps, kicks) will pop. Reproduce: node tools/shot.mjs rigaudit_sim --eval "__ED.sim.run('spin',{series:['t','hipsStep']})".
findings.evidence: hipsStep (mm per frame, model frame) for demo.combo3: 0.40:119 0.417:116 0.433:275 0.45:503 0.617:428 0.633:114 0.65:142 0.667:144. Max for the other clips: idle 1.6, walk 23.7, hit 47.5, slam 109 (its authored impact drop). Capture: shots/char/rig/sim_spin_pelvispop_sheet.png (split at 0.433, standing at 0.450, deep crouch at 0.617).
findings.suggestedFix: Drop the pelvis only for feet that are planted (target height < ~2 cm and IK weight ~1). Make the function continuous: clamp hz to R before computing, cap the drop (e.g. 0.12 x leg length) and low-pass it over time (critically damped, ~0.08 s). Let unreachable feet in the air use soft reach instead of moving the pelvis. Add a regression check that fails any clip whose max per-frame hips step exceeds ~60 mm unless it is keyed.

findings.title: Cape tunnels through the torso in the spin finisher at 60 Hz (17 frames, rendered cloth 11 cm inside, edges stretched 3.6x)
findings.detail: This happens even with the pelvis pops removed (lab clip 'audit.spin' = combo3 with the swing-foot circle x0.4, max hips step 31 mm). From t=0.467 to 0.733 (17 consecutive frames) rendered cape vertices are inside the torso capsule and structural edges pass through capsules. The cape folds into a flat dark band across the front of the chest plus a stiff slab at the waist, with a needle-like stretched edge to the floor. It gets worse at 30 Hz, with a 1/15 dt spike, with a timed facing turn and on the low tier (coarser 5x6 grid). Root causes in src/char/cloth.js. (1) Pins are interpolated across substeps (279-285), but body capsules are evaluated at the END-of-frame pose for every substep, so a fast torso jumps past particles. (2) Collision runs once per substep, after all Gauss-Seidel iterations (311-321), so the constraints drag particles back into the body. (3) pushOutCapsules (collide.js:45-66) pushes to the NEAREST surface, so tunnelled particles are pushed out of the wrong side and the sheet tears. (4) The 14 m/s velocity clamp is saturated for 11 frames (vmax 14.0-14.5), so the cape cannot keep up with the 16 rad/s spin. At 60 Hz there are only 2 substeps (273). README section 7 claims 'long-range tethers (no runaway stretch)'.
findings.evidence: Clean spin at 60 Hz: rpen 29-37 vertices (17 f), rdepth 0.111 m, edges 14 (17 f), stretch 3.63x, particle pen 3 (1.9 cm). hz30: rpen 33, stretch 3.4-3.6x. Spike 1/15: stretch 5.4x. Timed turn: stretch 7.7x, rpen 54 (13 cm). Low tier spin: rpen in 33 frames, depth 0.150 m. hz120: rpen 0, stretch 1.39 (fine). Lab-only copy of Cloth.update (__ED.sim.experiment()): capsule lerp alone gives no gain; collision in the last 3 iterations gives rpen 5 / stretch 2.46. Capsule lerp + collision in the iterations: spin rpen 0, stretch 1.61, cost p10 0.65 ms (vs 0.55). Plus a max substep of 1/240 s: spin/hz30/spike all rpen 0, stretch 1.24-1.41, but cost 1.08-1.14 ms per character. Captures: shots/char/rig/sim_cleanspin_34_sheet.png, sim_cleanspin_top_sheet.png, sim_cleanspin_close_0.583.png.
findings.suggestedFix: In Cloth.update: interpolate capsule endpoints per substep exactly like the pins (keep last frame's capsule data). Run pushOutCapsules inside the last 2-3 constraint iterations, not only after them. Push out along the side the particle was on in the previous substep, not the nearest surface. Use adaptive substeps: 2 normally, 4 when max pin/capsule speed exceeds ~3 m/s, to stay inside the 1 ms budget. Raise or scale maxSpeed during fast moves.

findings.title: Cloth and spring bones are not time-step consistent: different swing at 30/60/120 Hz, limp cape and over-fast plume in slow motion
findings.detail: src/char/cloth.js: damping is applied per SUBSTEP (`damp = 1 - s.damping`, line 274) and the number of substeps depends on dt (`dt > 1/55 ? 3 : 2`, line 273). So damping per second and solver iterations per second change with frame rate: 90 / 120 / 240 / 1200 substeps per game second at 30 Hz / 60 Hz / 120 Hz / 0.1x. Verlet velocities (p - pp) are not rescaled when the substep length changes (cloth.js:289, spring.js:66). When slow motion starts, the per-frame displacement is carried into frames 10x shorter, so the cloth keeps real-time speed for a few frames and then becomes almost frozen (0.965^1200 damping per game second). Springs show the same carry-over. This violates CONTRACT 'animation, cloth and VFX must look identical at 60 fps and when a frame is dropped (dt 1/30)'. Ultimates and skill finishers use slow motion 0.2-0.6 (MOVES.md). Hit-stop (dt = 0) itself is clean. Every cloth/spring parameter tuned now will be wrong after the fix, so fix before content authoring.
findings.evidence: Free swing after a 0.25 m root jolt (__ED.sim.decay()), cape hem zero-crossing: 30 Hz 0.20-0.25 s, 60 Hz 0.37-0.45 s, 120 Hz 0.40-0.50 s, 0.1x never (creeps back over 1.5 game s = 15 s real). Slow motion entered mid-swing (dtCompare): cape hem game-time speed in the first 50 ms is 13.35 m/s vs 3.0 m/s in the 1x run (4.5x). Plume tip 18.4 vs 8.7 m/s in the slow-motion window (2.1x). Cape RMS deviation from the 60 Hz run at equal game times: uniform 0.1x 0.42 m, 120 Hz 0.25 m, 30 Hz 0.16 m. Hit-stop deviation is 0.0034 m (clean). Lab variant 'all' (time-based damping + time-corrected Verlet + 1/240 substeps) gives zero-crossings of 0.20-0.30 s at all of 30/60/120 Hz and 0.1x. Captures at equal game times 0.30-0.55: shots/char/rig/sim_slowmo_ref1x_sheet.png (cape flares) vs sim_slowmo_01x_sheet.png (cape hangs straight down).
findings.suggestedFix: Damping per second: damp = pow(1 - c, h / h_ref) or exp(-k h). Time-corrected Verlet: on the first substep, v = (p - pp) * (h / h_prev). A fixed substep length with an accumulator (or XPBD compliance) keeps stiffness independent of dt. Apply the same to SpringChain: track the previous dt and rescale (p - pp). Re-tune the knight's cloth/spring parameters afterwards.

findings.title: A single NaN input poisons the character: impulse NaN is permanent, others persist until teleport() (no spring failsafe)
findings.detail: impulse({amount: NaN}) or impulse({dir: [NaN,0,0]}) writes NaN into the flinch springs (index.js:409-427, stepped in additive() 460-477). Nothing ever resets them: teleport() (index.js:527-532) resets cloth and springs but not springsBody / boneSprings. Result: all 188 bones are non-finite forever and the fighter vanishes for the rest of the match. setClipTime(NaN), play(name, {speed: NaN}) and root.position.x = NaN for ONE frame leave the character non-finite for at least 1 s of idle: the SpringChain tips keep NaN forever (spring.js:49-97 has no failsafe, unlike Cloth). They recover only after a manual teleport(). update(NaN), update(-1/60), lookAt(NaN vector) and wind NaN are handled. No NaN occurred in any normal scenario (19 scenarios, 0 NaN frames, 0 failsafe resets).
findings.evidence: __ED.sim.robust() on fresh characters: impulse_amount_NaN and impulse_dir_NaN give finiteAfterIdle1s false, finiteAfterTeleportPlus1s false, 188/188 bones non-finite. setClipTime_NaN, play_speed_NaN, root_position_NaN_one_frame: finite only after teleport().
findings.suggestedFix: Guard public inputs with Number.isFinite (play speed/fade/startAt, setClipTime, impulse dir/amount, lookAt target, wind, update dt). Add a NaN/explosion failsafe to SpringChain.update (reset like Cloth) and to the flinch springs. Make teleport() also zero springsBody and boneSprings.

findings.title: Flinch impulses accumulate with no clamp: head whips 37-55 deg in multi-hit moves, 178 deg under spam
findings.detail: impulse() adds angular velocity to unbounded springs (index.js:409-427, 460-477). Multi-hit moves in MOVES.md (Iska 6 slashes, Vorn 9 bolts, Kael 3 rapid cuts) will call impulse per hit. The README's suggested launcher value 'amount 2-3' already gives a 53 deg head whip.
findings.evidence: Deviation from the same frames without impulses (__ED.sim.robust()): single amount 1: chest 5.9 deg, head 17.6 deg (README says ~8 / ~12). Amount 3: chest 17.6, head 52.7. 9 hits every 6 frames: head 37.1. 6 hits every 4 frames: chest 14.3, head 54.9. 30 consecutive frames: chest 55.1, head 178.4, hips shove 0.28 m.
findings.suggestedFix: Saturate the spring state with a soft clamp (e.g. tanh to ~20 deg torso, ~35 deg head, 5 cm shove). Scale each new impulse by the remaining headroom so flurries read as a sustained flinch instead of an accumulating whip.

findings.title: teleport() / cloth reset costs a 13.6-16.4 ms frame and snaps the cape through a rotated torso; springs are not pre-settled
findings.detail: (a) After teleport() or the cloth failsafe, the next update runs the 24-step pre-settle for each cloth (cloth.js:250-253), which drops a frame on desktop and several on phones. (b) _snap hangs the cloth from 'rest offsets below the pinned row, unrotated' (cloth.js:235-247). If the torso is yawed (mid-move), the rest drape points through the body and the settle pushes particles out of the nearest side, so the cape visibly jumps. (c) SpringChain.reset only restarts the tips at the rest direction, so the plume falls and swings for ~4 s after every reset or spawn. Mid-move teleports are in the design brief (Iska skill3 blink, Vorn Arc Step).
findings.evidence: __ED.sim.parts(): updateAfterTeleportMs 16.36 vs updateMs_idle 1.0. robust(): 13.6 vs 0.84 ms. A fresh character's first update is 36.4 ms. teleportReset during the clean spin: cape speed 71.6 m/s, jerk 1260 mm vs 14.7 m/s / 218 mm in the same spin without the reset. Capture shots/char/rig/sim_teleport_reset_sheet.png: the cape jumps from wrapped around the torso (0.450) to hanging straight down on the camera side (0.467). Plume speed at rest after a reset: 1.1 m/s at 0.35 s, 0.08 at 2.0 s, 0.002 at 4.0 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Reset by rigidly carrying the last cloth shape into the new pose, or express the rest drape in the anchor bone frame so it rotates with the chest. Cut or amortise the pre-settle (e.g. 4-6 steps, or spread over frames). Pre-settle spring chains to their gravity equilibrium. Document the cost of teleport() and prefer the automatic >0.6 m detection, which is artefact-free (3 m jump: no extra stretch or penetration).

findings.title: Mixer eviction pop: a 5th state discards the fully weighted base pose instantly (1.56 m weapon-tip jump in one frame)
findings.detail: index.js:202 `while (states.length > 4) statePool.push(states.shift())` drops the OLDEST state, which is the base (always blended at weight 1). The next state, whose weight may still be near 0, becomes the base and the pose snaps to it. This happens whenever more than 3 play() calls land inside one fade window: restart hit reactions in multi-hit moves, cancels, or a hit then knockdown in the same frame.
findings.evidence: robust().mixer_eviction: 0.5 s fades started every 2 frames. Per-frame weapon-tip motion 0.123 0.085 0.142 0.160 0.183 0.164 then 1.555 m at the 4th play (eviction of the base), then 0.395 m at the 5th, against 0.08-0.18 m normally.
findings.suggestedFix: On overflow, bake the two oldest states into one snapshot pose (blend with the current weight, then keep it as a frozen base that fades out), or evict the lowest-weight non-base state. Expose the cap in the README.

findings.title: Spring bones ignore animation although the docs say they follow it
findings.detail: spring.js:57 builds the target from rig.restRot (the bind rest) instead of the bone's animated local rotation lq[i], so keys on spring bones have no effect. README section 7 says 'pulled to the animated direction' and the design table says 'stiffness (1/s^2 toward the animated direction)'. Authors cannot lift tassets during high kicks or lunges, aim the plume, or key straps.
findings.evidence: robust().spring_bone_keyed_rotation: a held pose keying tassetR [0,0,60] changes the bone by 0.03 deg; plume1 [0,0,70] changes by 0.15 deg (after 180 settle frames).
findings.suggestedFix: Use the sampled clip rotation as the spring target: target model rotation = mq[parent] * lq[i] before simulation (keep restRot as the fallback when unkeyed). Then add a test and fix the README.

findings.title: Timed facing turn tears the cape (stretch 5.9-7.7x) although the README says cloth is unaffected
findings.detail: setFacing(f, {turn}) mirrors the root and spins root.rotation.y through 180 deg in `turn` seconds (index.js:517-524, 598-602). computeInertia feeds this rotation to the cloth as real inertia (index.js:569-578). So the cape is swept through the torso during the presentation spin. README section 2: 'turn > 0 (seconds) spins through a quick turn instead. Cloth / springs are unaffected.' Side switches after cross-ups are normal play.
findings.evidence: flipTurn scenario (turn 0.15 s at t=0.30 / 0.80, clean spin): cape stretch 5.9-7.7x, rpen 52-57 vertices, depth 0.13-0.14 m, edges 25-30. The instant-flip variant shows no extra damage (same numbers as the plain spin). Even with every cloth fix in experiment() it is still rpen 14-17, stretch 3.3-3.4. Capture shots/char/rig/sim_flipturn_sheet.png.
findings.suggestedFix: Exclude the turn's own rotation from the inertia transform (it is a presentation trick, not world motion), or clamp the angular part of the inertia per frame (e.g. <= 8 deg). Fix the README sentence.

findings.title: Plume spring has no collision and droops 5.5 cm into the back / helmet at rest
findings.detail: knight.js plume spring: collide: false, gravity 0.45 vs stiffness 50, and the design has no head or back-of-helmet collider. The plume settles into the helmet's neck guard and the upper back, so the signature crimson plume is mostly swallowed in the silhouette and clips in close-ups. In moves it reaches 4-8 cm inside the torso/shoulder capsules. Note: knight.js is the rig engineer's demo design, not an ART file.
findings.evidence: rest scenario: plume depth 0.055 m in 323/360 frames (from t=1.5 s onward). spin 0.051, slam 0.044, slowmoSlam 0.078 m. Captures shots/char/rig/sim_plume_rest_back_3.000.png (plume mostly hidden inside the helmet/gorget) and sim_plume_rest_side_3.000.png.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a helmet capsule and an upper-back capsule to the colliders and enable collide on the plume. Raise stiffness or lower gravity, or bake a rest pose that arcs up and back. Design guideline for Kael/Iska/Vorn: every spring chain gets colliders for the body parts it can reach.

findings.title: Per-frame allocations (~7 KB per update) despite README 'No per-frame allocations in update()'
findings.detail: Measured by heap growth without GC over 50-100 updates in steady state. Main sources: TypedArray.subarray views, which allocate even in optimised code (measured 60 B each), in solveLimb (ik.js:79-81 and 87: 6 per call, ~10-14 calls per update), resolve (index.js:277, 312), update (index.js:621) and Cloth.update (cloth.js:266). Others: the closure `toLocal` created every update (index.js:583) and Map iterators in additive() (index.js:474) and applyLayers (index.js:381). Math.hypot is NOT a source once optimised (0.3 B/call).
findings.evidence: CDP Runtime.getHeapUsage deltas: 50 updates 7650-7661 B/update, 100 updates 6819-7037 B/update (25-update runs include re-warm-up). That is about 0.42 MB/s per fighter at 60 fps. Micro-test: dst.set(src.subarray(4,8)) = 60.4 B/call. Scripts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user--/8256de2b-7eff-573b-8afc-504b52b3c9af/scratchpad/cdp/rate.mjs, micro.mjs, alloc.mjs.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace subarray copies with qcopy / explicit index loops, hoist toLocal to the factory scope, and iterate arrays instead of Map iterators. Then re-run rate.mjs and expect < 100 B/update.

findings.title: Unbounded dt: update(Infinity) never returns; huge dt emits thousands of events
findings.detail: advance() loops `while (s.time >= d) { s.time -= d; wraps++; }` (index.js:241), then emits every wrap (index.js:247-249). The app clamps dt to 1/15, so this needs a caller bug (e.g. passing time since pause). Negative speed on loops never wraps: clipTime goes to -2 after 2 s and freezes on the first key (index.js:240-242). Unknown clip names throw from play()/layer() (anim.js:311). A throw inside ctx.onUpdate aborts that frame's remaining updaters and render; the character itself stays usable.
findings.evidence: robust(): update(1e4) on demo.walkF took 2.5 ms and emitted 26,315 'step' events in one update. negative_speed_loop: clipTime -2.0 after 120 frames. play('no.such.clip') throws 'unknown clip no.such.clip'; after_throws_still_updates finite true.
findings.suggestedFix: Clamp dt at the top of update() (e.g. <= 0.25 s), wrap with modulo, emit at most one wrap's events, and support negative speed with a symmetric wrap. In production builds, warn once and fall back to the idle clip on unknown names (keep the throw under __DEV__).

findings.title: Lazy per-rig clip compilation on first play (no precompile API); a fresh character's first update costs 36 ms
findings.detail: getClip compiles each clip per rig on first use (anim.js:304-316). prewarm() only compiles shaders. With ~150-200 clips per fighter this means 0.1-0.9 ms hitches the first time each move is used mid-fight, and two instances of the same design compile everything twice. A new character's first update also runs both cloth pre-settles.
findings.evidence: __ED.sim.parts(): clip compile 0.1-0.9 ms per clip (combo3 0.9), 12 demo clips 4.5 ms total. firstPlayAndUpdateMs_combo3_freshRig 36.4 ms. createCharacter 117-156 ms (load time).
findings.suggestedFix: Add char.precompile(names | 'all') (or compile in createCharacter from a clip list in the design) and run one warm-up update at load. Share compiled clips between rigs with identical proportions.

findings.title: Shadow pass draws the full 56.9k-triangle character: 113.8k triangles and 6 calls per knight
findings.detail: Every slot mesh has castShadow = true (build.js:179). The shadow pass re-skins and draws everything, including the cloth lining and rim, fingers, rivets and gauntlet detail. Two knights take 227.7k of the 350k whole-game triangle budget (CONTRACT), leaving 122k for environment and VFX. A character at 6 calls is at the contract's per-character limit if the shadow pass counts.
findings.evidence: __ED.sim.draw(): charCalls 6 (3 main + 3 shadow), charTris 113,836, shadowTris 56,918. Vertices: plate 39,456, suit 4,644, blade 3,043. Bone texture 28x28.
findings.suggestedFix: Build a low-poly shadow proxy per character (merged, a few k triangles, same skeleton) and set castShadow = false on the detailed meshes. Alternatively drop the cloth lining and small trims from the shadow pass via a separate slot.

findings.title: Mid tier (phones) runs the full desktop cloth; cost headroom will vanish once cloth collision is fixed
findings.detail: quality.cloth is 1 on both 'mid' (8-core phones) and 'high' (core/util.js), so mid phones run the 9x12 cape + 5x7 tabard with 10 iterations. Cloth is about 60-70% of the update cost. The substep fixes needed for SIM-02/03 roughly double the cloth cost.
findings.evidence: __ED.sim.cpu({n:3000}) on a 2.1 GHz Xeon (load average 10-14, so the best batch and p10 are the reliable figures). High: best 0.52 ms, p10 0.54-0.56, p50 0.62-0.93 ms per update; cloth ~0.32-0.40 ms of it. Low (cloth 0.5: cape 5x6, 8 iterations): best 0.18-0.20, p10 0.21-0.25. Two characters scale linearly. experiment(): 1/240 substeps give p10 1.08-1.14 ms. A control workload on the same machine showed p99 at 5x its median, so tail percentiles here are environmental.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cloth 0.7-0.75 on mid, adaptive substeps only during fast moves, and fewer iterations on the tabard. Re-measure on a real mid phone with #fpsmeter.

findings.title: Spring bones get a velocity kick after hit-stop; tasset tip clips into the thigh when legs cross
findings.detail: (a) During dt = 0 frames, SpringChain.update still applies the length / cone / collision constraints but leaves pp untouched (spring.js:63-87). The accumulated correction becomes velocity on resume, so the tassets jolt after every hit-stop. Cloth returns early on dt <= 0 and is clean. (b) pushOutCapsules handles capsules sequentially (collide.js:48-63): pushing a tasset tip out of one thigh can leave it inside the other when the legs cross.
findings.evidence: dtCompare hitstop (2 s freeze at t=0.36, clean spin): tasset deviation from the uninterrupted run up to 0.090 m at t=0.40; cape 0.028 m, plume 0.0097 m. Tasset tip depth inside a thigh capsule 0.065-0.085 m for 1 frame at t=0.45 in every spin variant.
findings.suggestedFix: On dt <= 0, return early (as Cloth does) or set pp = p after the constraints. Iterate pushOutCapsules 2x, or resolve against the deepest capsule last.

findings.title: Two fighters' cloth passes through each other: no inter-character or external collider API
findings.detail: Capsules are per character only, so A's cape and tabard pass through B's body in cross-ups, pass-through skills (Iska skill3, Vorn Arc Step) and cinematics with body contact (Vorn ULT 'victim lifted on the spear', orbit shots around both). The cloth is otherwise stable while overlapping (no NaN, no explosions).
findings.evidence: crossup (B walks through A): 43 of A's cape particles inside B's capsules (depth 0.158 m, 62 frames); B in A: 30 (0.161 m, 71 frames). A spinning with B at 0.9 / 1.2 / 1.5 m: 24 / 3 / 0 particles (depth 0.154 / 0.034 / 0 m); at 0.9 m the bodies themselves overlap after the 0.5 m root motion. Capture shots/char/rig/sim_spin_near_opponent_sheet.png.
findings.suggestedFix: Add char.setExternalColliders(list) (or addColliders(otherChar)) feeding world-space capsules into the cloth and spring push-out (12 capsules: negligible cost). Enable it in cinematics and close range.

findings.title: Simulation thresholds are hard-coded for the 1.9 m human (colossal-boss roadmap)
findings.detail: Thresholds that do not scale with the design: teleport/inertia-skip at 0.6 m per frame (index.js:566), cloth failsafe |p| < 50 (cloth.js:326), pre-settle 24 x 1/60 s (cloth.js:252), floor-contact ramp 0.06-0.25 m (index.js:632), default cloth maxSpeed 14 m/s (cloth.js:164). For an ~8 m boss (x4.2): a scaled Vorn-style dash of 8 m/s x 4.2 = 34 m/s is 0.56 m/frame, right at the threshold, so inertia toggles on and off frame to frame. A 4.7 m cape's pendulum period is ~2x longer (sqrt(4.2)), so 0.4 s of pre-settle leaves it swinging. A 4 m-radius cape swing at the same angular speed exceeds 14 m/s and gets clamped.
findings.evidence: Code references above; arithmetic from the boss scale in CONTRACT.md (7-9 m) and the measured human cape speeds (11-14 m/s in the spin).
findings.suggestedFix: Derive the thresholds from a design scale (rig.P.hipHeight / 0.98): teleport distance, settle duration, floor ramp and default maxSpeed. Document per-design overrides.

findings.title: Cape sags 5.5% at rest (edge stretch above the 4% tether)
findings.detail: With 10 iterations x 2 substeps the structural constraints do not fully hold the cape's weight; edges at rest sit at 1.055x their rest length (tabard 1.005x). This is polish: it elongates the hem slightly and softens the drape. The tether limit is 1.04 (cloth.js:164, 312-315).
findings.evidence: rest scenario: cape stretch 1.0546 in all 360 frames (tabard 1.0048). Rest jitter is excellent: cape 0.0008 mm, tabard 0.0004 mm, tasset 0 mm per frame after 4 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply tethers inside the iteration loop, or use a stiffer stretch pass (two passes of vertical edges). It becomes free with XPBD / the substep changes of SIM-03.
